It began on March 4 and ended on December 2. ==General== ===Promotion/relegation=== * At the end of the [[2005 J.League Division 2|2005 season]], [[Kyoto Sanga FC|Kyoto Purple Sanga]], [[Avispa Fukuoka]], and [[Ventforet Kofu]] were promoted to J1. * At the end of the [[2005 J.League Division 1|2005 season]], [[Kashiwa Reysol]], [[Tokyo Verdy|Tokyo Verdy 1969]], and [[Vissel Kobe]] were relegated to J2. * At the end of the [[2005 Japan Football League|2005 season]], [[Ehime FC]] was promoted to J2. ===Changes in competition format=== * The Division 2 was expanded to 13 clubs. * In games that require [[extra time]] in case of a tie (i.e. two-legged league cup games) [[away goals rule]] is adopted. ===Changes in clubs=== ''none'' ==Honours== {| class="wikitable" |- !Competition !Champion !Runner-up !3rd place |- |[[J1 League|J.League Division 1]] |[[Urawa Red Diamonds]] |[[Kawasaki Frontale]] |[[Gamba Osaka]] |- |[[J2 League|J.League Division 2]] |[[Yokohama FC]] |[[Kashiwa Reysol]] |[[Vissel Kobe]] |- |[[Emperor's Cup]] |[[Urawa Red Diamonds]] |[[Gamba Osaka]] |[[Kashima Antlers]]

Marinos]] | {{flagicon|Brazil}} [[Dutra (footballer, born 1973)|Dutra]] | {{flagicon|Brazil}} [[Marques (footballer, born 1973)|Marques]] | | | | {{flagicon|Brazil}} ''[[Magrão (footballer, born 1978)|Magrão]]'' |} == Format == Eighteen clubs will play in double round-robin (home and away) format, a total of 34 games each. A club receives 3 points for a win, 1 point for a tie, and 0 points for a loss. The clubs are ranked by points, and tie breakers are, in the following order: * Goal differential * Goals scored * Head-to-head results A draw would be conducted, if necessary. However, if two clubs are tied at the first place, both clubs will be declared as the champions.
